searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he pass one — chessed brainstorm: the full movie universe the awtsmoos gives every instant a frame and every frame a door, so the first pass names the broadest useful movie world before choosing the core. ideal capability universe one canonical movie document containing metadata, duration, frame rate, aspect ratio, tracks, scenes, assets, actors, cameras, lights, audio cues, transitions, and render directives. scene graphs for 2d and 3d objects with stable ids so ai can reference and animate prior objects across time. keyframes with easing, spring, path, morph, opacity, transform, color, material, camera, and text property animation. procedural animation primitives: orbit, follow, pulse, float, shake, draw on, typewriter, count up, reveal, wipe, stagger, parallax, explode, implode, flow, bounce, and particle emitters. character primitives: silhouette people, rigged/basic 3d people where available, sprites, labels, speech bubbles, entrances, exits, gestures, look at, walk paths, grouping, and reusable cast ids. 2d educational visuals: rectangles, circles, arrows, connectors, timelines, diagrams, callouts, progress meters, bar/line/pie charts, counters, grids, icons, equations, highlighted text, and step by step tutorial overlays. 3d visuals: boxes, spheres, cylinders, planes, text meshes, groups, lights, particles, camera rigs, environment colors, and procedural geometric assemblies. camera language: wide, medium, close, over shoulder like framing, top down, orbit, dolly, truck, pedestal, zoom/fov, rack like focus approximation, handheld jitter, and cuts between named cameras. scene language: cold open, title, explainer, montage, data section, character section, demonstration, climax, recap, credits. ai compiler that turns natural language or structured json into deterministic movie operations with schema validation and repairable errors. asset references that accept existing urls/data assets without requiring media generation to demonstrate animation capability. audio timeline metadata for narration/music/sfx even when the current runtime cannot synthesize audio itself. export oriented deterministic timeline stepping so future video capture/rendering can reproduce exact frames. ux universe mobile first: bottom action rail, large touch targets, single column prompt/editor mode, swipeable scene strip, full screen preview, collapsible inspector. desktop: split preview/timeline/inspector while sharing the same semantic controls. ai entry: one prominent “describe your movie” control plus advanced json/spec import. scene cards: duration, type, thumbnail/preview color, object count, quick duplicate/remove/reorder. timeline: scrub, play/pause, jump scene, loop, fit, current time, total duration. object editing: tap/select, transform, visibility, timing, motion preset, style/material, text. safety: clamp invalid durations, missing ids, nan transforms, impossible camera targets, and unsupported object kinds into explainable validation errors. candidate shared architecture 1. apps/shared/movie/ as the engine neutral canonical movie package. 2. data model and validators independent of dom/three.js. 3. a 2d renderer adapter for canvas/svg/dom. 4. a 3d renderer adapter for three.js when available. 5. a timeline evaluator shared by both modes. 6. a command/program compiler used by ai facing surfaces. 7. per app persona presets so animator, video editor, mitzvah studio, and nesher studio can feel different while speaking the same movie language. possible app personalities animator: direct animation playground, object/timeline centric. video editor: composition/timeline/media centric. mitzvah studio: guided story/explainer/educational preset centric. nesher studio: cinematic 3d/camera/scene centric. failure map duplicate movie schemas drifting across apps. demo data hard coded into runtimes with no ai programmable path. timeline calculations diverging between 2d and 3d. browser runtime assuming desktop dimensions or mouse only input. three.js dependency loaded inconsistently or missing on a route. ai output trusted without schema repair/validation. scene changes leaking objects or event listeners. 180 second demo existing only as documentation rather than runnable data. concurrent agent overwrites causing regressions. what this pass intentionally does not decide exact files, exact compatibility strategy, and exact renderer ownership remain subject to repository inspection.
